newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: CEFTA seen starting talks with Bulgaria in July.
newsitem.headline: CEFTA seen starting talks with Bulgaria in July.

text.p: Membership negotiations between Bulgaria and the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) group should start in July, CEFTA's current president Slovenia said on Monday.

"Economic ministers of the CEFTA countries are expected to give the go-ahead for the start of negotiations at their meeting this week," Vojka Ravbar, Slovenian state secretary for international economic relations, told a news conference.
The ministers will hold a two-day meeting at Slovenia's Alpine resort of Bled on Thursday and Friday.
Slovenia, a former Yugoslav republic, has held CEFTA's rotating presidency since July. CEFTA also includes Hungary, the Czech Republic, Poland and Slovakia. Romania will become full member from July.
Ravbar said negotiations between CEFTA and Bulgaria could be finished as early as this year.
She also said Slovenian exports to CEFTA countries rose 11.7 percent to $450 million in 1996, while imports fell 3.3 percent to $613 million.
"Since 1993, when we started to prepare the first free-trade agreements with the CEFTA countries, our trade with those countries has doubled," Ravbar said.
Slovenia became a full member of CEFTA in 1995 but earlier signed separate free-trade agreements with all CEFTA states.
Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Macedonia and Ukraine have also said they would like to join CEFTA.
